mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 3.0% signals accommodative monetary policy that lowers equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporate valuation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 3.0%, or Rank IC over 5 years falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%, or Rank IC over 3 years falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll growth (PAYEMS rising) and unemployment decline (UNRATE falling) indicate labor market tightness that accelerates inflation, triggering monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or interaction effect p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.5% in 3 months), policy shifts reduce liquidity and increase discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% in 3 months, or Rank IC over 5 years falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1200 thousand units signal robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through increased consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST > 1200, or Rank IC over 3 years falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% triggers expectations of aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or Rank IC over 5 years falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous industrial production decline (INDPRO falling) and rising housing starts (HOUST rising) indicate supply-demand mismatch where supply constraints outpace demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO falls and HOUST rises, or interaction term p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In supply shock regimes (INDPRO falling below 105.0), manufacturing output contraction reduces corporate profits and drives negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0, or Rank IC over 5 years falls below 0.02.
